- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 3–8% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward — reduce forecast by 3–7% in next 3–5 days.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility or sentiment swings, dampen forecast by 1–4% per day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows high positive sentiment followed by low sentiment, model often fails to adjust — apply downward correction of 5–10% in 2–4 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon — reduce first 5–7 days by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underestimates — increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid under-shock.
